model_claims.text: "import x as y, a" makes isort treat every module on that line as alias-only.
model_claims.source_quote: `import x as y, a` makes isort treat every module on that line as alias-only.

model_claims.text: When you have `import x as y, a` followed by `import a as b`, isort produces `import a as b\nimport x as y`, losing the plain import `a`.
model_claims.source_quote:
import x as y, a
    import a as b

becomes

    import a as b
    import x as y

model_claims.text: With `remove_redundant_aliases=True`, `import a as a` next to `import a as b` loses the plain `import a` too.
model_claims.source_quote: with `remove_redundant_aliases=True`, `import a as a` next to `import a as b` loses the plain `import a` too.

model_claims.text: Lazy imports behave the same way.
model_claims.source_quote: Lazy imports behave the same way.

model_claims.text: The added test `test_plain_import_next_to_an_alias_is_kept_when_the_module_is_also_aliased` in `tests/unit/test_regressions.py` fails on main, passes with the fix.
model_claims.source_quote: Tests: added `test_plain_import_next_to_an_alias_is_kept_when_the_module_is_also_aliased` in `tests/unit/test_regressions.py` (fails on main, passes with the fix).

model_rejected_claims.text: `import a as b, a` and `import a, a as b` both become just `import a as b`.
model_rejected_claims.source_quote: `import a as b, a` and `import a, a as b` both become just `import a as b`.
